topics.title: Employment: people, participation and measurement
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Separate the labour force, workers and unemployed before interpreting a rate. This pilot covers selected concepts, not the entire unemployment chapter.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Government of India / Economic Survey 2025-26 (claimed)
The jobs discussion combines employment estimates, organised-manufacturing employment, portal registrations and vacancies. These measure different populations and events.
Separate employed persons from registered workers, advertised vacancies and training places before evaluating job creation; retain age coverage and reference quarter.

Portal registration or a vacancy is not a realised job. Labour-code recognition is not proof that benefits have reached every eligible worker. Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified.
World Bank / WDR 2026 (claimed AI theme)
The selected page prioritises foundational skills and warns that tax incentives favouring automation over hiring can affect labour demand.
Illustrative application: evaluate an AI subsidy by worker productivity, displacement, reskilling and access for small firms, not adoption alone.
This is a policy mechanism, not an India employment forecast. The claimed WDR theme and edition require official confirmation.

cards.question: Recall: why should e-Shram registrations, vacancies and employment counts not be added together?
cards.answer: They count different things, can overlap and use different periods or populations. Registration indicates administrative reach; employment requires a defined labour-market measure.

cards.question: Answer framework: can AI adoption generate inclusive employment in India?
cards.answer: Original planning prompt: define productivity versus displacement; examine foundational skills, firm information and finance gaps; assess tax incentives and worker transitions; conclude with productivity and job-quality indicators. Treat the compilation's policy discussion as unverified, not an observed outcome.

topics.title: Growth forecasts: publisher, period and revision
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Attach every forecast to its publisher, release and reference period. Different institutions' forecasts are not automatically conflicting observations of the same fact.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: IMF / WEO July 2026 update (claimed)
The compilation describes interim forecast revisions and a global baseline conditional on energy-market normalisation, trade policies and the technology cycle.
Compare India forecasts only after aligning publisher, release vintage, fiscal/calendar year and assumptions; test sensitivity to imported energy and external demand.
The detailed geopolitical baseline is unverified. A conditional projection is not an outcome; do not combine this global calendar-year projection with India's fiscal-year estimate.
Government of India / Economic Survey 2025-26 (claimed)
The page labels FY26 GDP and GVA numbers as First Advance Estimates and links demand to consumption and investment.
Use the estimate label and national-accounts concept; an advance estimate can change and GDP is not interchangeable with GVA.

Not a final realised growth rate; official national-accounts release and price basis should be checked. Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified.

cards.question: Application: an energy-shock assumption changes after a forecast. Must the earlier forecast be called an observed error immediately?
cards.answer: No. First identify the original conditional baseline, forecast horizon and later information. Compare the revised forecast or realised outcome on the same definition; do not silently replace the vintage.

facts.label: Global real GDP growth: calendar 2026, supplied July 2026 WEO compilation

observations.value: Compilation projects 3.0% global GDP growth in calendar 2026, conditional on its stated energy/trade baseline; not officially verified or a realised outcome.
observations.as_of: Purported July 2026 WEO update; forecast for calendar 2026

topics.title: Agriculture: food security, markets and resource trade-offs
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory sector breadth: connect nutrition, price discovery and farm incentives. Deepen scheme eligibility from official current sources; avoid memorising every old subsidy rate.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Government of India / Economic Survey 2025-26 (claimed)
Agricultural infrastructure, farm-gate facilities and electronic markets are presented as complementary channels for efficiency and price discovery.
Illustrative mechanism: storage and market access can reduce losses and improve sale timing, while price discovery needs actual participation and competition.

The page's trader-registration unit and the placement of a large transfer amount under pension discussion are ambiguous; neither claim is retained. Infrastructure access does not establish a causal income gain.
FAO with IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
Healthy-diet affordability depends on food-basket composition, local prices, value chains and productivity; local and seasonal differences can be hidden by national averages.
For India, complement cereal output and buffer-stock discussion with diverse nutritious foods, local market prices, logistics and household purchasing power.
India application is an analytical extension, not an India SOFI estimate. Cost of a Healthy Diet data coverage and update frequency are explicit limitations.

cards.question: Answer framework: why is foodgrain output insufficient evidence of nutrition security?
cards.answer: Original outline: distinguish availability, access, affordability and dietary diversity; connect productivity and value chains to local food prices; add household resources and targeted protection; monitor nutritious-diet costs rather than only aggregate tonnage.

topics.title: External sector: trade, capital flows and convertibility
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Explain how trade, financial flows and policy interact. Keep BoP accounting separate from claims about development; the source itself gives inconsistent convertibility dates, preserved for review.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) / WIR 2026 (claimed)
The compilation distinguishes FDI flows, multinational activity, greenfield projects and international project finance; its SDG investment discussion is uneven across sectors and countries.
Assess India investment by entry mode, sector, technology transfer and infrastructure additionality rather than headline inflow alone.

Announced greenfield projects, project-finance measures and balance-of-payments FDI are not interchangeable. No India inflow or sectoral ranking is inferred. Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified.

cards.question: Application: does a rise in announced greenfield project value prove an equal increase in realised FDI?
cards.answer: No. Project announcements, financing and realised investment differ in timing and coverage. Evaluate completion, financing conditions and sectoral allocation before inferring development benefits.

topics.title: International institutions: mandate, finance and reports
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory globalisation breadth plus objective report knowledge. Match institutions to functions and reports; do not memorise mutable membership counts from undated notes.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: IMF / WEO July 2026 update (claimed)
WEO is presented as a macroeconomic outlook with full reports and interim revisions, covering growth, inflation, fiscal and external indicators.
Use WEO for forecast-vintage and policy-risk comparisons, not as evidence of a lending commitment to India.

The page's '190 member countries' is not retained as current membership; verify institutional facts separately. Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified.
World Bank / WDR 2026 (claimed)
WDR is described as an annual thematic development analysis offering policy insights, rather than a standard short-run macro forecast.
Use thematic mechanisms to structure development answers, distinguishing them from IMF projections and UNCTAD investment tracking.
The supplied AI title and team attribution are not independently authenticated and should not be memorised as official edition facts.
FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
SOFI is attributed to a joint UN-agency assessment of hunger, food insecurity, diet quality and nutrition targets under SDG 2.
Choose food and nutrition evidence suited to the question; do not treat all international reports as measuring the same development outcome.
Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified. This attribution is recorded from the PDF, not independent publisher confirmation.

cards.question: Recall: which analytical question is the supplied WIR framework best suited to?
cards.answer: Cross-border investment flows, multinational enterprises and investment-policy choices. It is not a household nutrition survey or a comprehensive macro forecast; the supplied 2026 edition remains unverified.

topics.title: Growth and development: output, distribution and transformation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: distinguish real output expansion from inclusive development; explain productivity and structural change, then test jobs, capabilities and environmental costs rather than dumping GDP figures.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: World Bank / WDR 2026 (claimed)
AI gains require education, electricity, connectivity, affordable computing and accessible information; technology adoption alone is insufficient.
Illustrative India application: pair digital infrastructure with small-firm access, local-language tools and foundational learning to broaden productivity gains.
Examples such as UPI and IndiaAI in the compilation do not demonstrate measured causal effects. No return-on-investment estimate is supplied or inferred.

cards.question: Answer framework: distinguish a technological growth opportunity from inclusive development.
cards.answer: Original outline: identify the productivity channel; identify access complements and distributional barriers; assess employment incentives and public infrastructure; evaluate learning, firm reach and worker welfare, not only output.

topics.title: Human development: capabilities, human capital and feedback
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: explain real freedoms as the end of development, human capital as a productive means, the growth–capability feedback loop and why average index gains can hide exclusion.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Joint UN agencies / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
The selected pages call for coordinated health, agriculture, education and social-protection policies to make healthy diets affordable.
Use a capabilities chain: affordable diverse diets support health and learning, while income security and service access determine whether households can benefit.
The causal chain is an original analytical application, not an estimated effect in this PDF. Global findings are not India prevalence figures.

cards.question: Application: income rises but nutritious foods remain locally costly. Is human development guaranteed?
cards.answer: No. Real access depends on prices, diet composition, local availability and public services. Combine income measures with nutrition and service indicators; avoid treating national means as every household's experience.

topics.title: Sustainability: resource limits, policy and intergenerational equity
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: connect present needs with future resource availability, explain growth–environment mechanisms, evaluate policy instruments and SDG implementation without treating an income threshold as automatic environmental repair.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: SDG Report 2026 compilation / UN framework attribution not independently checked
The text prioritises timely, disaggregated, nationally owned statistics, confidentiality and methodological independence; AI should support rather than replace statistical standards.
For India, assess district and group disparities and retain methods, survey periods and revision notes when tracking SDG-linked programmes.
AI interpolation is not equivalent to observed data. The compilation's report identity and global progress percentages are not verified; numeric progress claims are omitted.
UNCTAD / WIR 2026 (claimed)
The selected discussion separates telecommunications, renewables and lagging social/infrastructure sectors; aggregate recovery can conceal unequal investment.
An India sustainability assessment should examine water, sanitation, health and education funding alongside energy and digital investment.
Global sector patterns are not India findings. Project counts, values and completed assets differ; no reported growth percentage is promoted to a verified fact.

cards.question: Recall: which safeguards are lost if AI-generated estimates are treated as observed official statistics?
cards.answer: Provenance, transparent methods, accountability and representation can be weakened. Preserve independence, confidentiality, community inclusion and clear identification of modelled versus observed values.

cards.question: Answer framework: can rising investment alone establish SDG progress?
cards.answer: Original outline: identify sector allocation and financing mode; examine completion and access; test who benefits and which sectors lag; pair capital measures with social and environmental outcomes. Treat the PDF's 2026 trends as unverified.

topics.title: Poverty: incidence, depth, capabilities and vulnerability
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: distinguish absolute, relative and multidimensional poverty; interpret incidence versus shortfall, trace poverty traps and match persistent deprivation or temporary shocks to suitable policy responses.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Government of India / Economic Survey 2025-26 citing World Bank (claimed)
The page discusses a revised international poverty threshold using a new PPP price base and separately names extreme and lower-middle-income poverty.
When comparing Indian poverty estimates, align threshold, PPP vintage, survey/reference year and population coverage before interpreting change.
A threshold/PPP revision is not itself a welfare gain. The compilation's poverty rates are not retained as verified estimates; do not splice rates across definitions.
Joint UN agencies / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
Least-cost healthy-diet measures illuminate a deprivation channel that calorie availability or aggregate income alone may miss.
Illustrative India application: evaluate food-price shocks using local nutritious-basket prices and household purchasing capacity, including vulnerable groups.
Diet unaffordability is not identical to an income-poverty headcount; geographic and seasonal price gaps limit national-average interpretation.

cards.question: Application: can rates computed at different PPP vintages be compared as a pure change in poverty?
cards.answer: Not without a harmonised series. First align the poverty line, PPP base, survey welfare measure and reference year; separate methodological revisions from changes in household circumstances.

topics.title: Demography: population change, dependency and the dividend
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: separate natural increase from migration, interpret crude rates and age composition, and explain why a demographic opportunity produces growth only with health, skills, participation and productive jobs.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: MoHFW / IIPS, NFHS-6 (claimed)
The compilation groups fertility and contraception with district-level population, health and family-welfare measurement.
Keep fertility behaviour, service access and population age structure distinct when discussing India's demographic transition and dividend.

Internal period inconsistency: page 3 says '2023-24' but its phase dates extend to December 2024. Survey coverage wording is malformed. Fertility and contraception figures are excluded pending official verification.

cards.question: Recall: why should contraception coverage and total fertility rate be kept conceptually separate?
cards.answer: Contraception is a service/use indicator; fertility summarises childbearing. Neither directly measures labour-force skills or employment. The supplied NFHS-6 values and period require verification.

topics.title: Health: prevention, access and financial protection
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory syllabus breadth: explain health as well-being and a development input, distinguish prevention from treatment and financial protection from service availability, and prepare one coherent delivery-reform answer.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: MoHFW / IIPS, NFHS-6 (claimed)
The tables distinguish antenatal contacts, skilled/institutional delivery, postnatal care, child nutrition and insurance/financing coverage.
Evaluate the care continuum and financial protection separately: insurance coverage does not establish service quality or freedom from out-of-pocket costs.
NFHS-6 edition, comparator values and survey timing are unverified; page 3 contains conflicting period descriptions. No coverage percentage or causal scheme attribution is endorsed.
Joint UN agencies / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
The text links maternal/child nutrition and healthy diets to health, education, agriculture and social protection.
Use preventive nutrition and affordable diverse food as complements to clinical care, not substitutes for treatment or health-system capacity.
Global discussion only; it does not identify a measured India programme effect. Supplied secondary compilation only; official edition and underlying evidence have not been verified.

cards.question: Application: can wider health-insurance enrolment prove universal health coverage?
cards.answer: No. Assess access, quality, continuity and financial protection in addition to nominal coverage. Use the supplied tables to classify indicators, not to assert the unverified NFHS-6 percentages.

topics.title: Education: access, learning and equitable opportunity
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Mandatory syllabus breadth: distinguish forms of learning, enrolment and meaningful educational opportunity; explain access–quality–equity and prepare a reform answer that separates policy aspirations from achieved results.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: World Bank / WDR 2026 (claimed)
Literacy, numeracy, reasoning, digital skills and teamwork are presented as foundations for adapting to technological change.
For India, combine advanced-technology skills with foundational learning and affordable connectivity; evaluate equitable readiness rather than course counts alone.
Policy recommendation, not an observed learning gain. AI theme and report edition remain unauthenticated.
Government of India / Economic Survey 2025-26 (claimed)
The selected education discussion describes credit frameworks, academic credit records and flexible entry/exit alongside school access.
Ask whether flexible pathways improve progression, recognition and inclusion; enrolment and institutional expansion alone do not measure learning.
The school-ratio sentence has an omitted indicator label and later labels it GER; institution counts and scheme naming are not independently checked. Numeric and naming claims are not reused.

cards.question: Answer framework: how should India prepare students for AI-linked labour-market change?
cards.answer: Original outline: foundational literacy and numeracy; digital access and reasoning; adaptable skills and transitions; information for firms and students; assess participation, learning and employment quality rather than training enrolment alone.

topics.title: Gender: agency, resources, care and participation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Core depth: use health, education, work and representation as distinct lenses; explain how norms, unpaid care and asset control shape agency, then evaluate an equity-oriented policy mix without relying on one headline ratio.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: MoHFW / IIPS, NFHS-6 (claimed)
The compilation separates internet use, phone ownership/use, operating a bank account, cash-paid work and household decision participation.
Illustrative India application: assess resources, actual use, paid-work opportunity and decision-making jointly; a bank account is not proof of control over household resources.
Definitions and denominators differ. Do not equate 'worked in last 12 months and paid in cash' with PLFS participation. All NFHS-6 percentages and new-module claims remain unverified.

cards.question: Application: a woman has a bank account and phone. Does that establish economic agency?
cards.answer: No. Distinguish ownership, independent use, income opportunity and control over decisions. These are separate indicators in the supplied table; do not infer causation or equate them to labour-force participation.

topics.title: Public expenditure and receipts: classify before evaluating
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Separate accounting classification, economic purpose and financing consequences when assessing public finances.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Ministry of Finance / Union Budget 2026-27 (claimed)
The compilation distinguishes estimated receipts/expenditure, revenue/capital categories and Budget versus Revised Estimates.
Classify each fiscal item before evaluating development priorities; compare BE with BE or explicitly identify the change in estimate status.

Capital spending is not automatically effective and revenue spending is not automatically waste. The introductory classification is broad; legal authorisation and accounting treatment require primary documents.

cards.question: Recall: why must a fiscal comparison retain BE, RE and actual-status labels?
cards.answer: BE is a budget plan; RE revises that plan as information improves; neither is a final outturn. A change in the estimate label can otherwise be mistaken for a realised spending change.

topics.title: Public debt: financing, risk and sustainability
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Evaluate debt using its use, servicing burden, maturity and currency risk rather than a single headline ratio.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: NITI Aayog / FHI 2026 assessing FY2023-24 (claimed)
The framework separates liability/GSDP, interest/revenue and a growth-versus-interest-payments-growth measure; these capture different fiscal pressures.
For Indian states, combine debt stock with debt-service burden and revenue capacity, considering structural differences and transfer dependence.
Do not replace the PDF's interest-payments-growth indicator with the textbook interest-rate-minus-growth formula. Ratios and index weights require official methodology verification.

cards.question: Application: can two states with equal debt/GSDP face different repayment pressure?
cards.answer: Yes. Compare interest burdens relative to receipts, own-revenue capacity, committed expenditure and reliance on transfers. An identical stock ratio does not imply identical fiscal space.

facts.label: Centre debt/GDP: FY2026-27 BE, supplied Budget compilation

observations.value: Compilation reports 55.6% of GDP for central debt in FY2026-27 BE; unverified projected ratio, not general-government debt or an outcome.
observations.as_of: Union Budget 2026-27 compilation; FY2026-27 BE (no exact release date asserted)

topics.title: Fiscal policy: deficits, stabilisation and consolidation
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Link the budget's allocation, redistribution and stabilisation roles to deficit measures, financing choices and policy trade-offs.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Ministry of Finance / Union Budget 2026-27 (claimed)
The selected fiscal table separates fiscal, revenue and primary deficits and central debt ratios, with FY2026-27 BE beside FY2025-26 RE.
Evaluate consolidation by the type and quality of adjustment, not only a deficit headline; retain the central-government scope and estimate status.
Budget estimates are not realised outcomes. Reported deficit and debt values are stored only as dated, unverified observations below; official budget tables were not checked.
IMF / WEO July 2026 update (claimed)
The policy discussion favours temporary, targeted support for vulnerable households over broad subsidies and conditions withdrawal on normalising markets.
Illustrative India application: weigh household protection, fiscal cost, price signals and exit design when responding to an imported-energy shock.
Conditional general advice, not an implemented Indian measure or universal ban on support. The shock narrative and edition remain unverified.

cards.question: Answer framework: design a fiscally credible response to an energy-price shock.
cards.answer: Original outline: identify transmission to inflation and real incomes; target temporary household relief; assess fiscal space and incentives; set an exit trigger; coordinate monetary and financial-stability policy. Do not present the PDF recommendation as implemented Indian policy.

facts.label: Centre fiscal deficit: FY2026-27 BE, supplied Budget compilation

observations.value: Compilation reports 4.3% of GDP for the Centre's FY2026-27 Budget Estimate; unverified plan, not an outturn.
observations.as_of: Union Budget 2026-27 compilation; FY2026-27 BE (no exact release date asserted)

topics.title: Federal finance: powers, sharing and intergovernmental support
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Distinguish tax assignment, tax sharing, grants and borrowing constraints within India's fiscal federation.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: 16th Finance Commission / recommendation period FY2026-27 to FY2030-31 (claimed)
The compilation distinguishes vertical sharing between Union and states from horizontal distribution among states, and excludes cesses/surcharges from its divisible-pool explanation.
Explain fiscal imbalance and interstate equity separately; an increase in the gross tax take need not translate proportionately into the divisible pool.
Recommendations do not establish acceptance or implementation. The claimed 41% share is excluded pending official report/acceptance verification.
NITI Aayog / FHI 2026, FY2023-24 reference data (claimed)
The framework separately evaluates major states and North-Eastern/Himalayan states, adding transfer and committed-spending measures for structural differences.
Interpret interstate comparisons alongside terrain, revenue base and service-delivery costs rather than reading a single ranking as effort alone.
Publication label 2026 is not the fiscal reference year 2023-24. No rank or score is endorsed; cohort coverage and methodology require primary confirmation.

cards.question: Recall: distinguish vertical and horizontal devolution.
cards.answer: Vertical devolution sets the collective state share relative to the Union; horizontal devolution allocates that state share among individual states. Keep the two stages separate; this PDF's numerical recommendations remain unverified.

topics.title: Banks and RBI: development, inclusion and policy transmission
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Separate financial intermediation from central-bank policy and evaluate whether formal access becomes usable, resilient finance.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: RBI / Financial Stability Report June 2026 (claimed)
FSR is described as a collective assessment of financial-system risks and resilience; the microfinance section juxtaposes recovering credit with a shrinking borrower base.
Do not infer universal inclusion from sound aggregate balance sheets or expanding credit; examine reach, borrower stress and interconnected institutions.
Report edition is not the period of every indicator. An unspecified 'latest quarter' is not assigned a date; no stress or borrower count is endorsed.

cards.question: Recall: is the supplied FSR framework an assessment of financial stability or proof of inclusive credit access?
cards.answer: It assesses systemic risks and resilience, drawing on regulator inputs. Inclusive access requires additional borrower and distribution evidence; strong aggregate resilience alone does not establish it.

topics.title: Rural credit and microfinance: access with borrower resilience
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Match financing to rural cash flows and compare formal institutions, group finance and borrower-protection risks.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: RBI / FSR June 2026 (claimed)
The microfinance discussion distinguishes credit growth, borrower numbers, multiple-lender exposure and arrears; these can move in different directions.
Illustrative India application: credit growth with fewer borrowers may mean larger balances or concentration, not broader outreach; evaluate affordability and repayment capacity.
A shrinking borrower base need not prove exclusion caused by regulation. The quarter and dataset behind the counts are not clear; no causal or numeric claim is promoted.

cards.question: Application: microfinance lending grows while borrower numbers fall. What should an inclusion answer ask?
cards.answer: Check active borrowers, average exposure, multiple borrowing, overdue loans and pricing. Distinguish reduced over-indebtedness from reduced access; aggregate lending alone cannot settle which dominates.

topics.title: Inflation: measurement, causes and limits of policy
topics.subject: ESI
topics.summary: Identify the relevant price measure and shock before explaining monetary transmission and the growth-price trade-off.

tables.title: Report evidence: framework, India application and verification

cells: Joint UN agencies / SOFI 2026 (claimed)
Cost of a Healthy Diet estimates the least cost of a nutritionally adequate basket, subject to price coverage and update limits.
For India, use it as a nutrition-affordability lens alongside, not in place of, CPI; local and seasonal price differences matter for household vulnerability.
A diet-cost level is not a CPI inflation rate. Do not compare PPP-denominated cost levels across years without checking price bases and methodology; global values are omitted.
IMF / WEO July 2026 update (claimed)
The policy discussion links persistent inflation, expectations and exchange-rate pass-through to a tighter stance, while easing is conditional on weaker growth and subsiding price pressure.
Illustrative India application: distinguish a first-round supply shock from second-round inflation and choose policy conditional on persistence and credibility.
Not an RBI policy decision or an automatic rate rule. General recommendations and the purported July 2026 context remain unverified.

cards.question: Application: can healthy-diet affordability worsen even if headline inflation slows?
cards.answer: Yes. Slower inflation need not lower the price level or raise household purchasing power. Diet composition, local prices, availability and income matter; use the PDF framework rather than an invented India statistic.
